name: worktree-write-scope-decisions
body:
Reconciliation record for change-set `worktree-write-scope`. (1) C1 — source: "every generated agent grants permission.edit on root main paths AND apg/.worktrees/*/ mirrors; root cause agent-builder rule 10". Verified: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` lines 155-162 ("Worktree mirroring (MANDATORY)") and 325-338 (rule 10) mandate root+mirror; `.opencode/agents/implementer.md` grants `"src/*.rs": allow` (l.28) and `"opencode-suite/**": allow` (l.47) at root alongside `apg/.worktrees/*/src/*.rs` (l.50). Inconsistency: existing nodes `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`, `requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations`, `domain.value.permission-scope`, `domain.constraint.fs-operation-scope-enforced` encoded root+mirror, contradicting the approved worktree-only model. Resolution: amended all four in place to worktree-only for code-writers; added `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes` + `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`, `domain.constraint.worktree-only-write-scope`, `domain.entity.worktree-write-boundary`, `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`. [with user] (model approved by the user). (2) C2 — source: "fsScopeDecision resolves candidate against caller directory; agentFsGlobs reads root-relative edit allow globs". Verified at `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` (apg.ts 156-193) and `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs` (252-282). Resolution: folded into the code-writer requirement's ACs (single frame + main-resolving path refused) rather than a separate requirement, since it shares the same law and test surface [autonomous]. MECHANISM LEFT TO THE PLAN [autonomous]: options include (a) resolve the candidate to absolute and match against grants anchored at the main-checkout root (the session root opencode uses), refusing any absolute path not under `
/apg/.worktrees/

/`; (b) derive the main root from the worktree (`findApgRoot` / git common dir) and refuse candidates under main but outside `apg/.worktrees/`; (c) strip the `apg/.worktrees/*/` prefix and match worktree-relative. The law only requires one frame and a structural main refusal. (3) C3 — source: navigator grants `git merge/checkout/switch/rebase/worktree *` (verified codebase-navigator.md lines 71-79). Per-verb decision [autonomous]: drop merge (bypasses verify gate — `apg project merge` owns it), drop checkout/switch (move main HEAD; flow never needs them), narrow worktree to `git worktree list *` (add/remove owned by `apg project start`/merge self-clean), keep rebase (agent-builder main-flow sync; run inside worktree), keep read-only status/diff/log/branch. Residual risk: `git rebase *` is pattern-cwd-agnostic, so the "inside the worktree" rule is prose-enforced; recorded in `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only`. (4) Release-agent — source: "main-write set is repo-specific, analysed by agent-builder, confirmed via interview; no hardcoded list". Existing `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent` and `domain.entity.release-agent-flow` listed "(version files, formulae, changelog, …)" as the scope without stating main or per-repo derivation. Resolution: amended both to main-checkout scope, per-repo analysis + interview, no worktree mirror, examples only (not a law). [with user]. (5) `requirements.constraint.main-write-carve-outs` NOT created [autonomous]: it would duplicate `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`, which names the carve-outs. (6) Out of scope: the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are NOT edited; they are regenerated by the agent-builder on main AFTER merge + `apg init` + opencode restart (a follow-up, not a requirement). [with user]
